Stripping out QQQB, whose zero maker fees and a new VIP volume multiplier drove the spike, July volume was $2.03 billion, about 30% below June's total.

title: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
blurb: Bank of Italy tested 200 USDC transfers across 10 remittance corridors and found total costs ranged from 0.3% to nearly 9% of the amount sent, with blockchain fees a tiny fraction and exchange fees, FX spreads, and local banking charges driving the bulk. The research concludes stablecoins solve on-chain speed but not the costly last mile between crypto and local fiat.

title: Bitcoin cold-wallet attack spreads to 4,500 addresses as losses near $89 million
blurb: Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of wallet sweeps exploiting weak keys from a March 2021 Coldcard firmware build, bringing total losses to 1,367 bitcoin, nearly $89 million, across 4,585 addresses. The latest wave targets smaller balances averaging a tenth of a bitcoin each and uses harder-to-trace transaction patterns, sending funds to unique pay-to-witness-script-hash outputs instead of shared collector addresses.

title: Bitcoin mining difficulty shrinks 14% from this year's high as plunging revenues force operators to pivot
blurb: Bitcoin mining difficulty fell to 126.23 trillion, roughly 14% below its January peak and 19.1% off the November 2025 record high, as compressed revenue and capital shifting toward AI infrastructure cut network capacity. Hashprice sank to $27.66 per petahash per day in late June before recovering to $31.7, with Luxor's forward market pricing $31.85 through year-end, signaling little economic relief for remaining miners.

title: XRP Ledger upgrade brings back features once pulled over critical bugs
blurb: The XRP Ledger's xrpld 3.3.0 release, expected next week, asks validators to approve five amendments, including revised Batch and Permission Delegation features that were withdrawn earlier this year after researchers found bugs enabling unauthorized transactions or fee draining. Batch executes up to eight cross-account transactions atomically and Permission Delegation grants scoped signing authority, both needing 80% validator approval over two weeks to activate.

title: Coinbase's weak quarter leaves Wall Street split on timing of a recovery
blurb: Coinbase missed second-quarter expectations across nearly every major metric, reporting $1.22B in revenue and $208M in adjusted EBITDA as depressed crypto prices and subdued trading volumes weighed on transaction and subscription revenue, sending shares down 6%. Analysts pinned the miss on one of the weakest trading environments in years rather than execution, and remain split on whether volumes rebound soon enough to support earnings growth despite a record 10.3% share of global crypto trading volume.

title: Dubai-based crypto exchange tied to $4 billion Iran sanctioned-evasion network
blurb: Reuters reported that Shelbit, an unlicensed Dubai-based crypto exchange run by Iranian expatriate Siavash Kayvanpour, sits at the center of a $4 billion sanctions-evasion operation that moved hundreds of millions of dollars through platforms including Binance for Iran's central bank and other sanctioned entities. Binance said Shelbit never held an account, that related transactions weren't flagged high-risk, and that it froze linked accounts and reported them to law enforcement.

title: Marc Andreessen & Chris Dixon: Why America needs CLARITY
blurb: Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon argued on the a16z crypto show that the CLARITY Act, the market structure bill now moving through the Senate after passing the House with bipartisan support, is once-in-a-generation legislation that would set the ground rules for where the financial system and internet get built. They frame the status quo of regulatory ambiguity as the costlier option, pushing US crypto activity offshore rather than protecting it.

title: World Cup bets smash records as prediction markets hit $20 billion in volume
blurb: The 2026 FIFA World Cup generated a record $20 billion in prediction market volume across nearly 400,000 wallets since January, according to Chainalysis, with $5.7 billion traded during the tournament itself. The figure dwarfs the $3.6 billion placed on the 2024 US Presidential Election and lands as market leader Polymarket sits at a $15 billion valuation and rival Kalshi targets $40 billion.

title: U.S. sanctions Iran-linked bitcoin insurance scheme for Strait of Hormuz ships
blurb: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned two Iranian maritime firms, Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and HormuzSafe Marine Services Authority, over an alleged extortion scheme that accepted bitcoin and other digital assets to let ships transit the Strait of Hormuz and funneled proceeds to the IRGC. The designations bar U.S. persons from dealing with the firms and expose crypto-paying foreign companies to secondary sanctions.

title: Everyone has the perps convergence backwards
blurb: In a CoinDesk opinion piece, Bitget CEO Gracy Chen argues the convergence narrative is inverted: rather than crypto maturing toward traditional finance, traditional assets are migrating onto perpetual futures, the market structure crypto invented. Real-world-asset perp volumes hit a record $211B in May 2026, roughly 16x their ~$12B level in Q4 2025, with equity perps up 121% month over month to $54B. The draw is continuous, globally accessible markets settled onchain, with no borrow desk to short and no contract to roll.

title: Bitcoin Lags Stock Rally After Hawkish Fed Hold
blurb: Bitcoin fell 3.5% to $62,464 as it sat out Friday's stock rally, with the S&P 500 up 1.7% and Nasdaq up 2.8% after the Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on a 9-3 vote. June PCE inflation ran at 3.7% and Q2 GDP grew 3.0%, pushing the rate cut bulls expected further out and leaving crypto without its catalyst into August.

title: Binance founder CZ calls for wallet diversification after $70 million Coldcard exploit
blurb: An attacker drained roughly 1,082 BTC, worth about $70 million, from 1,196 Coldcard wallets by exploiting a March 2021 firmware flaw that weakened recovery-seed randomness and let private keys be reconstructed offline. Binance founder CZ responded by urging holders to split funds across multiple wallets, reviving debate over self-custody limits after even a long-established hardware device harbored an undetected critical bug.

title: RWA perps will outpace tokenization
blurb: DWF Labs' Martin Lee argues that perpetual futures on real-world assets are scaling faster than tokenization, citing $347B in RWA perp volume in May, a 1,472x jump from January 2025, and $4.5B in daily DEX open interest by July. His case rests on 24/7 settlement and simpler mechanics than TradFi futures and options, with perp holders compounding at roughly 33% a month against spot's 17%.

title: Bitcoin, ether fall, equities rally with broader crypto market on track for best month in a year
blurb: The broader crypto market is on track for its best month since July 2025, with the CoinDesk 20 index up 8.7% since June, even as bitcoin fell 1.31% to $63,870 and ether dropped 1.40% to $1,890 on July's final day. Crypto diverged from equities as South Korea's Kospi surged over 15% and Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.23%, while UNI gained 9.30% on Robinhood layer-2 momentum.

title: Tether posts $1.5 billion operating profit in Q2 as reserve buffer falls by half
blurb: Tether reported $1.5B in Q2 net operating profit, driven by returns on its US Treasury and repo holdings, even as excess reserves fell by half to $4.11B from $8.23B a quarter earlier. The buffer shrank as Tether added 14 tons of gold and roughly 1,800 bitcoin to reserves whose mark-to-market value dropped alongside falling gold and bitcoin prices, against $184.6B in USDT outstanding.

title: Coinbase Says Revenue From Its Base Layer 2 Fell Despite Record Volume
blurb: Coinbase said "other" transaction revenue fell 11% quarter-over-quarter to $47.4M, largely from lower Base sequencer fees, even as stablecoin volume on the L2 grew sevenfold year-over-year to roughly $32T in trailing-12-month transfers. The deliberate trade-off routes users toward USDC, where Coinbase captured about 50% of economics and booked $292.1M in stablecoin revenue, though overall Q2 revenue of $1.22B missed estimates on a third straight net loss.

title: An investigation reveals Dubai-based unlicensed crypto exchange Shelbit has processed at least $4B as part of Iran's sanctions-evasion operation since May 2024 (Reuters)
blurb: A Reuters investigation found that Shelbit, an unlicensed Dubai-based crypto exchange, has processed at least $4B since May 2024 as part of Iran's effort to move money around US and international sanctions. The findings put fresh scrutiny on offshore exchanges operating outside KYC/AML regimes and hand FinCEN and OFAC a concrete target as regulators tighten oversight of crypto-based sanctions evasion.

title: Fintech broker Clear Street offers investors pre-IPO access to $188 billion AI giant Databricks
blurb: Clear Street is close to launching a platform that lets accredited investors buy into late-stage private companies, starting with Databricks at a $188B valuation, via SPVs that hold stakes through third-party funds rather than direct shares. The structure carries real counterparty risk, since Databricks says it has no relationship with Clear Street and rivals like Anthropic have voided unauthorized SPVs, though Cohen says his firm will stand behind the deals.

title: Circle secures New York trust charter as crypto regulatory push accelerates
blurb: Circle secured a limited-purpose trust charter from the NYDFS, authorizing the USDC issuer to provide fiduciary, custody, and asset-management services under New York banking law. The charter follows Circle's OCC approval this month to establish a national trust bank, and joins Coinbase, Paxos, and BitGo in stacking state-level authorizations that tighten oversight of USDC's $71.8B reserve and position issuers for institutional custody mandates.

title: SEC to review Nasdaq bitcoin options approval after CME challenge
blurb: The SEC froze Nasdaq PHLX's approval of QBTC cash-settled bitcoin index options to reconsider the decision after CME Group challenged it, arguing that bitcoin is a commodity whose derivatives fall under CFTC jurisdiction, not the SEC's. The outcome will define which regulator governs crypto options, and could force Nasdaq to register as a CFTC-regulated venue or redesign the contracts, with comments due by Aug. 24.

title: Bank of Italy research suggests stablecoins aren't necessarily cheaper for remittances
blurb: Bank of Italy tested 200 USDC remittances across 10 corridors and found total costs ran from 0.3% to nearly 9%, with exchange fees, FX spreads, and local banking charges, not blockchain fees, driving the expense. The research concludes stablecoins solve on-chain speed but not the costly "last mile" between crypto and local fiat, undercutting the cheaper-remittances pitch while noting always-on settlement remains a real edge.

title: U.S. sanctions Iran-linked bitcoin insurance scheme for Strait of Hormuz ships
blurb: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned two Iranian firms, Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and HormuzSafe Marine Services Authority, for running a bitcoin-settled maritime insurance scheme that Treasury calls extortion, forcing ships through the Strait of Hormuz to buy coverage and routing proceeds to the IRGC. The OFAC designations expose foreign companies that pay in crypto to secondary sanctions, extending Iran-related enforcement directly into digital-asset settlement rails.

title: Repeat founder Ryan Williams raises $10M seed for an AI startup for private credit managers
blurb: Ellis AI emerged from stealth with $10M in seed funding, led by investors including First Round Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Thrive Capital, to build AI agents that centralize the fragmented document, spreadsheet, and accounting workflows private credit managers run through Excel. Founded by Cadre co-creator Ryan Williams, the platform connects to a firm's existing systems to flag data discrepancies and automate portfolio monitoring, reporting, and month-end close while keeping human experts on material decisions.

title: New York alleges Kalshi is running an 'illegal gambling operation' in new lawsuit
blurb: New York's attorney general sued Kalshi, alleging the prediction-market platform runs an illegal gambling operation by offering sports and event contracts without a state gambling license. The suit adds to a mounting multi-state legal front against Kalshi, which claims federal CFTC oversight preempts state gambling law, leaving its exchange model and expansion plans exposed to conflicting jurisdictional rulings.

title: AI financial advice is surprisingly good, especially if you ask right questions
blurb: A new MIT Sloan paper found that AI chatbots like GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3 Flash give financial advice that reliably builds savings buffers for most people over 30, correctly pushing them to diversify, save during working years, and cut stock exposure after 45. The models fell short on adjusting to shocks like unemployment and let portfolios drift instead of rebalancing, with advice quality varying by prompt phrasing and user financial literacy.
